name: Battle of the Caudine Forks
intro: In the hills between Capua and Beneventum, 321 BC, in the Second Samnite War. You are the consuls Titus Veturius Calvinus and Spurius Postumius Albinus, with an army of perhaps 40,000 men camped near Calatia. The Samnite general Gavius Pontius is nearby.
debrief: In Livy’s account, Pontius sent soldiers dressed as shepherds to tell the Romans that the Samnite army was besieging Luceria. The consuls took the short road through the Caudine Forks, found both gorges blocked with trees and rocks and the Samnites on the heights, and after failing to break out, surrendered. The army was disarmed and sent under a yoke of spears, and 600 knights were given as hostages. Rome later refused to honour the peace. There was little fighting: the Romans lost to hunger and the ground. The other choices are what-ifs.

win: The legions break out of the valley.
lose: The army passes under the yoke.
Six hundred knights are left as hostages.
Rome will never forget the Caudine Forks.

decisions.title: Shepherds’ news
decisions.text: Shepherds captured near Calatia all tell the same story: the whole Samnite army is besieging Luceria, far away in Apulia. You are the consuls Veturius and Postumius, camped near Calatia.

hint.text: Every shepherd tells exactly the same tale.

scout.text: Ten men with the same story, word for word, may have been told what to say. Check before you march.

choices.label: Believe them and march to save Luceria

fx.text: You decide to march at once to save Rome’s allies in Luceria.

choices.label: Send scouts toward Luceria before marching

fx.text: Your scouts find no Samnite army near Luceria. Someone is lying.

choices.label: March, but by the longer road along the coast

fx.text: The long road is slow, but open.

decisions.title: The short road
decisions.text: The quickest way to Apulia runs through the Caudine Forks: a narrow gorge, then a grassy valley ringed by wooded hills, then another gorge.

hint.text: The valley has only two ways out.

scout.text: A valley with two narrow exits is a trap if anyone holds them.

choices.label: Take the short road through the gorge

fx.text: The army files through the first gorge into the green valley.

choices.label: Send troops to hold both exits first

fx.text: Your cohorts climb to the far gorge and find Samnites already building a barricade. They drive them off.

choices.label: Take the long road round the hills instead

fx.text: The army loses days, but stays out of the hills.

decisions.title: The way is blocked
decisions.text: At the far end of the valley, the gorge is blocked with felled trees and boulders. Samnites appear on the heights. You turn back, and the first gorge is blocked too.

hint.text: The Samnites have the heights; you have the valley floor.

scout.text: Try to break through one of the barricades while the army is still strong.

choices.label: Dig a camp in the valley and wait

fx.text: With the far exit in your hands, the army camps and waits for the Samnites to come down.
The army digs a camp on the valley floor while the Samnites watch from above.

choices.label: Storm the far barricade with everything

fx.text: The legions throw themselves at the barricade and tear a way through, under a rain of missiles.

choices.label: Climb the hills to attack the Samnites

fx.text: Men die on the slopes, but the Samnites give a little ground.

decisions.title: Hunger
decisions.text: Days pass. Food runs out. Every attempt to break out fails. The Samnite general Gavius Pontius waits.

hint.text: Your men are starving, but still armed.

scout.text: Make one more attempt while the men still have strength, before hunger decides.

choices.label: Send envoys to ask for terms
Make a last attack on the barricade at night

fx.text: The way through is still open. The army marches out by night.
In the dark, part of the army forces the barricade.

choices.label: Kill the pack animals and hold out longer for help from Rome

fx.text: The army eats its mules and holds on.

decisions.title: The terms
decisions.text: Pontius offers your lives: the army must give up its arms, leave six hundred knights as hostages, and pass under a yoke of spears.

hint.text: Pontius’s father advised him either to free you all with honour or kill you all.

scout.text: Living men can fight again; dead ones cannot.

choices.label: Accept, and pass under the yoke

fx.text: The army gives up its arms and passes under the yoke, stripped to their tunics. Rome has never been so shamed.

choices.label: Refuse, and die fighting rather than be shamed

fx.text: The army dies fighting in the valley.

choices.label: Bargain for time while scouts search the hills

fx.text: The bargaining wins time, and some men slip out armed.
